finding.statement: The elder Berkhamsted John is eliminated on his own age - fathering from 1597 puts his birth about 1570-75, twenty-five to thirty years before the colonial John - and that ground is immune to the same-name masking problem that weakens eliminations built on continuing residence. He holds at about 1 percent. The younger is a documented man of the right age whose household is documented dying rather than leaving, and he holds at about 4 percent. For him: the head himself has no recorded burial, inside a register window known to be defective. Against him: no Mary Gurney is baptised in the parish at any date, no John Gurney marriage occurs anywhere in the county in the window, and a Richard Gurney was buried in the parish in June 1638 who may well be his own son.

finding.statement: Across every surname stem and every father's forename, the Great Berkhamsted baptism corpus contains no Mary Gurney at any date between 1544 and 1888; the only Mary Gurney in the parish is a burial of 1730. Mary Gurney married Daniel Shed at Braintree, Massachusetts in 1647 and was therefore born by 1631 at the latest, which is the one primary bound in the colonial child set. This is the single strongest objection to the younger Berkhamsted John, and it operates at parish level rather than at household level, so it cannot be explained by a mis-assigned father.

finding.shortLabel: No John Gurney marriage anywhere in Hertfordshire between 1600 and 1654

sources.alignmentNote: The 1567 and 1646 Gurnett events are the coverage control that makes the 1600-1654 blank interpretable.
sources.locator: firstname=john&lastname=gurn* county-wide, 57 rows; and lastname=gurn*/gourn*&keywords=berkhamstead with the mirror spouselastname queries; authenticated session 28 July 2026

finding.statement: No John Gurn*/Gourn* marriage is recorded anywhere in Hertfordshire between 1600 and 1654. The county set's John Gurney marriages begin at Tring in 1655, with John Gurnett events at Cheshunt in 1567 and St Albans Abbey in 1646 bounding the negative on both sides, so the set is demonstrably carrying seventeenth-century Gurney-variant marriages across the window and simply holds none for a John Gurney. Great Berkhamsted's own Gurney marriages between 1582 and 1722 are all brides. The younger Berkhamsted John's wife therefore cannot be named from county records and cannot be tested against a Mary. A groom who married outside the county would surface in the south-Midlands archdeaconry licence series, which has never been searched.

incoming.explanation: The 4 percent is conditional on the June 1638 Richard not being his own son.
The register image is the first of the four settling records precisely because the burial reading is open.

outgoing.explanation: Only the four-household reading of the parish keeps the 1635 Thomas-household Richard in play as an alternative reading of the 1638 burial.

finding.shortLabel: The 28 June 1638 Richard Gurney burial: three readings, and only the register image discriminates

sources.alignmentNote: Bounds the set of candidate Richards.
sources.locator: Richard Gurney 1626 (father John) and Richarde Gurney 1635 (father Thomas); no other Richard Gurney baptism at Berkhamsted in the run

sources.alignmentNote: The transcript's own field set is the evidence that the index cannot resolve the question.
sources.locator: Transcript GBPRS/D/72723126, Richard Gurney, burial 28 June 1638, Berkhamstead, read 28 July 2026

finding.statement: A Richard Gurney was buried at Great Berkhamsted on 28 June 1638, and which Richard he is decides whether the younger John survives as a candidate at all. Three readings are open. He may be the Richard baptised there 15 December 1626 to a father John - in which case the candidate's best name-match child died in England at eleven while the colonial Richard Gurney of Weymouth was alive and a freeman into the 1680s, and the candidate collapses outright. He may be Richarde Gurney baptised 1635 to the neighbouring Thomas household, a three-year-old whose death in a mortality year is equally consistent with the entry. Or he may be an adult Richard of the parish never baptised there, which is the weakest reading, since no Richard Gurney baptism other than 1626 and 1635 appears in the whole run. The index cannot discriminate: the burial transcript carries name, date and place only, with no age and no parent. The register image normally gives 'son of', and it is the discriminator.
